I had to stop after the first two paragraphs. I am a veteran. My brother is a veteran, I go to the VFW and my friends are veterans. No one feels they get adequate care from the VA. The article uses a book that claims the VA provides the best care because it keeps patient records in house, so your care is referenced and monitored by the doctors. This is untrue. Each time you go to the VA, you see a different doctor, that recommends the same treatment the previous doctors did. Have a foot injury? The first doctor will put you in a brace and say if it doesn't work, surgery will most likely need to be performed.

After the brace comes off, your foot hasn't improved. You go back, and the second doctor puts you in a brace, and lets you know that if it doesn't work this time, surgery will be required. The third time, you get the same exact treatment. This is a true story, not a fabrication for an example.

Just like all things government, it looks great on paper. No one is arguing against the VA's treatments based on the outline, they are upset by the VA in practice.
